items.s: After three nights with no sleep, she felt completely ____ and could hardly stand.

items.s: Last Friday, I ____ home very late and fell asleep on the sofa.
She has ____ at her desk since nine o'clock.
The results of the study ____ in a science journal.

tfn.s: The study explains all kinds of tiredness.
tfn.why: The text says: "we should not treat it as an explanation for all tiredness."

tfn.s: Stress, poor sleep and illness can also cause tiredness.
tfn.why: The text says: "Stress, poor sleep, illness and many other things can also cause tiredness."

tfn.s: The tired people in the study preferred easier tasks, even when a harder task gave a bigger reward.
tfn.why: They were "less willing to choose a task that needed more mental effort, even when it offered a bigger reward."

tfn.s: Mental fatigue affects younger people more than older ones.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether younger or older people are more affected.

tfn.s: The writer says that people who feel tired after thinking all day are lazy.
tfn.why: The text says: "This does not mean we are lazy."

focus.note: Many adjectives and verbs are followed by one fixed small word. Learn the pair together, for example good at.

items.s: I'm tired ____ answering the same emails every day.
Thank you ____ helping me with the report.
I rely ____ coffee to get through the afternoon.
He's very good ____ planning his week.
She shared the housework ____ her brother.
The shop manager's ____ about next month's sales made it hard for him to plan.
Working two jobs for a year put a serious ____ on her health.
If you are unsure how much sleep you need, ask a doctor for ____.
Her apology sounded ____, so everyone believed she meant it.
Being busy does not ____ ignoring your friends.
Replacing every old computer in the building would be ____ for a small firm.

match.d: have no more of something left
continuing for a long time without stopping
identify what illness or problem a person has

items.s: By the time she got home, she ____ nothing since breakfast.
The experiment ____ in a university laboratory last year.
If you ____ enough tonight, tomorrow will feel even harder.
She avoids ____ her phone after nine o'clock.
While I ____ dinner, the phone rang.

tfn.s: The writer accepts that tiredness after mental work is a real experience.
tfn.why: The text says it "does not mean their tiredness is imaginary".

tfn.s: The 2025 study proved that people have a fixed supply of decision-making energy that runs out.
tfn.why: The text calls that popular explanation "too simple" and says it does not mean a fixed supply "has been used up".

tfn.s: Most of the participants in the study were university students.
tfn.why: The text gives the number of participants but does not say who they were.

tfn.s: The small size of the study and the many other causes of tiredness both mean it cannot be used to diagnose a person.
tfn.why: The experiment was "relatively small", tiredness "has many possible causes", and no such study "should be used to diagnose" exhaustion.

tfn.s: After they became fatigued, participants chose harder options more often when the reward was bigger.
tfn.why: They were "less willing to choose more demanding options, even when those options could bring greater benefits".

focus.note: After a noun or adjective, the preposition is usually fixed. Learn the whole phrase, not just the word.

items.s: A lack ____ sleep is a common cause of tiredness.
Too many late nights can result ____ poor concentration.
Your energy for the evening depends ____ how the day went.
Managers are responsible ____ setting realistic workloads.
Many people struggle to cope ____ constant interruptions.
No single request was unreasonable, but their ____ weight, added up over months, became unbearable.
Her explanation sounded ____, yet nobody could find any evidence to support it.
After a ____ illness that kept him in bed for several months, he returned to work part-time.
The panel was deliberately ____, including nurses, engineers and an artist.
Tired of old photographs, he preferred ____ art that reflected life in the present decade.
The first test was easy, but participants found every ____ test harder.

match.d: decide that something is not possible
real, and able to be seen or measured
aware of small but important differences

items.s: One small experiment offers little ____ for rewriting an entire company's break policy.
Persistent tiredness may point to an ____ medical condition rather than a busy schedule.
Doctors rarely draw a sharp ____ between mental and physical tiredness, since the two overlap.
It is wholly ____ to expect anyone to stay alert for ten hours without a proper break.
The ____ of conclusions drawn from only 28 participants is open to question.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that mental work can be undervalued because its effort is hard to see.
tfn.why: Employers judge effort by "visible hours", while cognitive work "is harder to observe" and can be "brushed aside as routine".

tfn.s: The writer treats the small sample as a reason to trust the study's conclusions more.
tfn.why: The text says "The small sample also limits how broadly its conclusions can be applied."

tfn.s: The participants in the study all worked in offices.
tfn.why: The text gives the number of participants but not their jobs.

tfn.s: The writer accepts that mental fatigue is real but warns against blaming it for every case of exhaustion.
tfn.why: The study's findings are taken seriously, yet "It would be a mistake" to attribute persistent exhaustion automatically to cognitive fatigue.

tfn.s: The writer sees the popular fuel metaphor and the study's conclusions as describing the same thing.
tfn.why: The study is "more nuanced" than the metaphor and concerns "not a simple depletion" of energy.

focus.note: Some phrases are fixed and cannot be guessed from meaning. Learn each noun or adjective with its preposition.

items.s: Doctors are reluctant to attribute persistent tiredness solely ____ overwork.
Each decision looks trivial ____ isolation, yet together they weigh heavily.
Symptoms like these are often indicative ____ a deeper problem.
Her insistence ____ regular breaks irritated her manager.
Many managers are preoccupied ____ visible hours.

speak.title: Role-play: who cooks tonight?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You've spent the whole day at a desk, answering emails and making decisions. You're exhausted and you don't want to cook or even choose dinner. Ask for help and suggest a simple plan.

b.text: You've had a busy day too, and you're hungry. You think sitting down all day isn't really tiring. Ask questions, then agree a fair plan for tonight and for the rest of the week.

phrases: I've had a really long day, and I can't think any more.
I know I've been sitting down, but my head is exhausted.
Could you choose something for dinner tonight?
I'd cook, but I've got no energy left.
How about we share the cooking this week?
That's fair, as long as we're both happy with it.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what plan did you agree, and who got the better deal?
